teaser: A second repository the agent cannot write to, which checks every release, trusts signed checks instead of re-running them, and is the only thing that deploys.
core_idea: A sidecar repository that no agent can write to holds the policy, a lock of approved hashes, private lists and keys, verifies GitHub's signed test results from the approved workflow instead of re-running them, waits for the owner when a gate changes, and is the only thing that deploys, so each attack by a fully compromised agent does nothing or stops the deploy.

Anything an agent can write, a compromised agent can rewrite.
the sidecar treats an agent's signature as attribution, never as a reason to skip a check

figures.caption: The sidecar, end to end: the agent pushes a release to the site's repository; its CI runs the tests and signs the result; the sidecar reads the commit, checks the paths against the policy, compares the workflow and tests with approved hashes, verifies the signed result, runs its own private checks, asks the owner when something in the gates changed, and deploys the site.

When the sidecar trusts a check and when it runs it again: if the workflow and every test file match the lock and the attestation is valid for the commit, the result is trusted and nothing is re-run; if anything in the gates differs, the owner decides, and the tests run again in the sidecar, without secrets.

What a fully compromised agent can try, and what the sidecar does: remove its hooks, nothing relies on them; rewrite the workflow or the tests, the lock differs and the owner decides; fake a status, ignored; forge a signed result, it fails verification; add a workflow to steal secrets, the site's repository holds none; bring back an old workflow, the lock differs; rewrite history, the sidecar deploys only from the last release; ring the doorbell, it reads the state itself; leak in content, the private lists catch it.
